title: World Models
tagline: Models that learn how an environment responds to actions, then plan or train agents inside it: model-based RL, Dreamer, MuZero, Genie, world foundation models, and JEPA-style planning.
prereqs: Reinforcement Learning and Generative AI: Images & Video. Self-Supervised & Contrastive Learning helps for the JEPA steps.

steps.title: What world models are
steps.why: The core idea: a learned model that predicts how a world changes after an action.

steps.title: Model-based reinforcement learning
steps.why: Learn a dynamics model from experience, then use it to plan or improve a policy.

steps.title: World Models (Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018)
steps.why: A VAE compresses frames, an RNN predicts the next latent, a tiny controller acts.

steps.title: Dreamer: learn behaviour inside the model
steps.why: DreamerV2 trains its actor and critic on imagined latent rollouts, mastering Atari.

steps.title: MuZero: plan with a learned model
steps.why: Its author explains a model that predicts reward, value, and policy, not pixels.

steps.title: Genie: worlds you can walk through
steps.why: The Genie 3 team on generating frames in real time from a user's actions.

steps.title: World foundation models
steps.why: Large video-trained models used to generate training data and test robots and cars.

steps.title: NVIDIA Cosmos, an overview
steps.why: NVIDIA's GTC 2025 introduction to its open world foundation model platform.

steps.title: Predict in representation space: LeCun's case
steps.why: Why LeCun argues world models should predict abstract features, not every pixel.

steps.title: V-JEPA 2: plan robot actions
steps.why: A self-supervised video model gets an action-conditioned predictor for robot planning.

projects: Recreate the 2018 World Models pipeline on CarRacing: train the VAE, the next-latent RNN, and a small controller, and compare a policy trained in the dream with one trained on real frames.
Train muzero-general on a small game such as tic-tac-toe or CartPole, then plot how often its learned-model rollouts predict the true reward a few steps ahead.
Learn a dynamics model for a Gymnasium environment from random play, then use it for model-predictive control and compare reward against a model-free baseline.
